statements.t: “The commencement of the TEMPO-1 trial marks our transition to late-stage clinical development, bringing us meaningfully closer to delivering sutantatug envedotin as a potentially novel, targeted therapeutic for those impacted by OPSCC who were previously treated with platinum-based and anti-PD1 therapy.
We look forward to presenting additional data at ObesityWeek®.”
The Company plans to engage with the FDA on the development plan and is also evaluating the potential to combine CRB-913 with GLP-1 therapy.

The Company had $115.3 million of cash, cash equivalents, and investments on hand as of September 30, 2026, which is expected to fund operations into 2028 based on current operating plans and planned expenditures.

There can be no assurance that TEMPO-1 will achieve its primary or secondary endpoints, that sutantatug envedotin will receive accelerated or full approval from the FDA, that previously reported clinical data, including topline data from CANYON-1, will be replicated in later-stage or larger controlled studies, that results of cross-trial comparisons will be confirmed, or that the Company will be able to obtain…
